subject: Acme Retail — AWS Private Offer: rev-share & billing term exceptions
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sam Hart <sam.hart@acme-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Retail — AWS Private Offer: rev-share & billing term exceptions

Marissa / Aditya / Laura — looping you in early. Acme (Sam Hart, procurement) is asking us to publish a AWS Private Offer this week for an enterprise purchase. Key asks from the customer: 

- 12-month commitment, $1.2M ACV (annualized).
- One-time onboarding discount: 15% off list for the first year.
- Marketplace commission: request that AWS take 25% (they want us to accept a 25% marketplace rev-share) — our standard marketplace rev-share is 20%.
- Billing terms: Net 90 (they are pushing for Net 90 via AWS marketplace invoicing).

Attachments: Acme-Deal-Summary-20281020.pdf, aws-private-offer-redlines.docx (I’ve marked the spot where they want Net90 and the commission note).

Why this matters: Acme is in active pilots with multiple product teams; this becomes referenceable retail account and opens potential expansion across 3 regions. Margin hit if we accept full asks: rough sketch in the attached impact-analysis.

Ask: I need an exception sign-off to move forward with the AWS Private Offer at the requested terms, or guidance on counter proposal we should present to the customer today. If we can’t do Net90, can we offer Net60 + payment cadence via AWS invoicing? If commission needs to be pushed to AWS at 25%, we should document finance reconciliation offsets here.

Please advise by EOD — Sam is hoping to lock dates with AWS listing next week.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(dylan.brooks@redwood.ai)

---
Attachment stubs: Acme-Deal-Summary-20281020.pdf (3 pages), aws-private-offer-redlines.docx (track changes)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Oct 2028 11:20:15 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Retail — AWS Private Offer: rev-share & billing term exceptions

Thanks for the summary, Dylan — quick clarifying points before we take to exec: 

1) The 15% onetime discount: is that across list for all seats/instances or just applied to the first invoice? We need the pricing table called out in the Deal Summary.
2) Commission math: our “standard” marketplace commission is 20% to AWS; increasing to 25% reduces net revenue significantly. Please include the break-even / margin impact in the XLS (I see a high-level tab but need line items per SKU).
3) Net90: we generally do not accept Net90 for customer-paid marketplace invoices without a credit application and finance approval. Net60 is sometimes doable for named accounts with a revenue holdback.

Counter proposals to consider if execs won't approve full asks: 
- Option A (preferred): Approve 12% one-time onboarding credit (instead of 15%), accept 23% rev-share to AWS (cap), offer Net60 with milestone-based payments.
- Option B: Hold rev-share at 20% (standard), give 15% credit but require upfront 50% prepayment for the first 3 months (or Net30 on AWS).

Aditya / Laura — can you weigh in on finance / legal feasibility? I’ll prepare a one-page deal memo if we have direction.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Deal Desk Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Aditya — escalating per Marissa’s note. Summary for exec ask: 

- Customer: Acme Retail (Procurement: Sam Hart).
- Request: 12-mo / $1.2M ACV; 15% onboarding credit; AWS marketplace commission 25%; billing Net90.
- Impact: If we accept full asks, FY28 net revenue reduces by ~18% vs list; gross margin compression on this bucket estimated at ~22 percentage points (see attached impact-analysis-aws-commission.xlsx).
- Upside: Reference customer with multi-region expansion; strong chance to convert pilot spend into 3x in year 2 if we land this listing.

Decision needed: 1) Approve the redlines as-is, OR 2) Approve a limited exception (see Marissa’s Option A / B) and instruct sales on counter-offer.

Time: Sam is pushing for a private offer creation window with AWS on Monday 10/23. If we miss that, we risk losing listing momentum.

Attachments: impact-analysis-aws-commission.xlsx (profitability by SKU + scenario analysis).

If you want a 5-min quick sync, I can hop on now.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Dylan / Marissa — I’ve reviewed the ask and the impact analysis. Given strategic value and go-to-market benefits, I’m prepared to approve a limited exception with the following conditions: 

1) Onboarding credit: approve 12% one-time onboarding credit (not 15%).
2) Marketplace commission: approve up to 23% rev-share to AWS (must be capped in the private offer metadata).
3) Billing terms: Net60 instead of Net90. For any Net60 requests, Finance will require a signed credit application and the first invoice paid via AWS invoicing before Net60 kicks in.
4) Legal: Laura, please confirm the tech addendum and the SLA language are included in the private offer. No exceptions to data residency or audit clauses without exec legal sign-off.
5) Finance: Marissa, please route the billing flow + HubSpot record to revenue ops to ensure accurate revenue recognition and marketplace reconciliation.

Dylan — once legal confirms, you have the green light to present the counter (12% onboarding / 23% rev-share / Net60 with credit app) to Sam. If the customer insists on Net90 or 25% commission, escalate back to me with CFO on CC.

This exception is approved on condition we get the formal tech addendum and HubSpot + DocuSign executed by 10/27/2028.

— Aditya
